newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks creep higher, reassured by strong NY.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks creep higher, reassured by strong NY.

text.p: Tokyo stocks crept higher in early Wednesday morning trade, reassured by strength in New York overnight as well as the stability of the yen, brokers said. As it was the first day of trade for June delivery, dealers were likely to be active, they said.
As of 0016 GMT, the 225-share Nikkei average was up 59.40 points or 0.30 percent at 19,949.29. Its June futures added 80 to 19,940.
"Hopefully, turnover will increase as we have started a new trading month," a broker at a middle-sized brokerage said.
Market sources said despite the pick up in buying interest, large gains for the main index were unlikely for the time being as profit-taking interest was strong above the 20,000 line.

"The Nikkei recovered to 20,000 in April and May in a corrective move following a sell-off which started late last year and went on until early this year," Masaaki Higashida, Nomura Securities strategist, said.
"But investors are now taking a deeper look at the economic environment for the second half of 1996/97," he added.
Brokers said a clue to the health of the economy could be revealed in the industrial production data due out Thursday.
In other indices, the TOPIX added 4.22 points or 0.28 percent to stand at 1,488.67. The Nikkei 300 rose 0.81 point or 0.28 percent to reach 288.07 by midday.
